headline: Memorial Boulevard arts magnet school project accepted as complete; 2027-28 and 2028-29 calendars approved
summary: Staff gave reports on state test scores, special education costs, and October enrollment. Nine policy items were approved, mostly to bring outdated rules up to date for a CABE audit. Student representatives also reported on school events and student concerns.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, items 8.1a to 8.2d. Motion carried.
Rescinded Policy 5145.6, Student Grievance Procedures Title IX. Motion carried.
Rescinded Policy 5145.5, Sexual Harassment/Exploitation. Motion carried.
Rescinded Policy 1112, News Media Relationships. Motion carried.
Adopted Policy 5142.4, School Resource Officer, as recommended. Motion carried.
Approved revised Policy 6164.12, Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. Motion carried.
Approved revised Policy 6114.3, Bomb Threats. Motion carried.
Approved revised Policy 6141.2, Separation of Church and State. Motion carried.
Approved revised Policy 1411, Law Enforcement Agencies. Motion carried.
Approved revised Policy 5118.1, Homeless Students. Motion carried.
Approved the 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 school calendars as presented. Motion carried.
Accepted the Memorial Boulevard arts magnet school project as complete and authorized the final payment request. Motion carried.
discussion: Special education tuition: Members said out-of-district tuition rates can rise after budgets are set, and suggested raising the issue with state legislators.
Financial dashboard: Staff demonstrated a new online budget tool, said a public version is planned, and asked members to keep their logins private.
Test score comparisons: Members asked how redistricting affects school results. Staff said students changed schools, so year-to-year school comparisons are not direct.
Kindergarten enrollment: Staff said a state cutoff date kept at least 66 children out of kindergarten seats this year.
School calendar: Members discussed a Wednesday dismissal problem that has lasted for years. Staff said fixing it would cut instructional time.
